slide_09_net.title: Net mining fell 90%, then came back
slide_09_net.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2014–2025 · thick bars and numbers: means for 2016–18, 2019–21 (shaded) and 2022–25
slide_09_net.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. Official SERNANP buffer-zone polygon. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_10_2019_parts.title: 2019: new pits kept opening, old ones went quiet
slide_10_2019_parts.subtitle: Net mining additions and parts, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2016–2022 · more stopping explains 25%–47% of the 2016–18 → 2019–21 fall; in Amarakaeri stopped land stayed flat (542 → 584 ha/yr)
slide_10_2019_parts.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. New land = mined for the first time since 1985; re-mined = mined again after a gap; stopped = left the mining class (water, regrowth). Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_11_region.title: The region kept growing, mostly in the legal corridor
slide_11_region.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr, period means · Madre de Dios · % = the legal corridor's share of the department's net additions (period sums) · legal corridor = all D.L. 1100 land, not only the strip across the road
slide_11_region.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. Legal mining corridor: D.L. 1100 polygon (INGEMMET), native communities excluded; legality is by location, the map class cannot tell legal from illegal. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_12_across.title: Across the road, net mining rose more than six-fold
slide_12_across.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr · corridor across the road (legal strip ≤ 10 km north of the highway) vs La Pampa sector (1,209 → 85 ha/yr) · 2014–2025 · thick bars: means
slide_12_across.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W (our boundary); corridor across the road = D.L. 1100 land at the same longitudes. We cannot show it was the same miners. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_13_money.title: Money faded after 2019, while gold rose 2.7-fold
slide_13_money.subtitle: Same years in each panel, 2014–2025 · PP 0128 executed spending booked in Madre de Dios (a lower bound) · gold price, nominal · net mining additions, Tambopata buffer zone · shaded: 2019–21 · context, not a test
slide_13_money.source: Source: MEF Consulta Amigable, PP 0128 devengado, Madre de Dios; World Bank Pink Sheet (nominal gold price, annual mean); MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. No correlation shown: 11 years, and money follows mining.

slide_14_came_back.title: It came back, partly on old pits (33–46%)
slide_14_came_back.subtitle: Net mining additions and parts, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2014–2025 · shaded: later years (2022–25) · share = re-mined ÷ (new + re-mined)
slide_14_came_back.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. 2023 is a spike in MapBiomas only (forest-loss alerts and Amazon Mining Watch are flat), so later years are shown with and without it. MAAP #193 (2023) reports miners back on degraded land. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_15_reserve.title: In 2025, mining inside the reserve jumped 241 ha
slide_15_reserve.subtitle: Net mining additions, ha/yr · Tambopata National Reserve (inside the reserve, not the buffer zone) · 2014–2025
slide_15_reserve.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. Platform check: 777 ha of mining inside the reserve in 2025 (protected-area statistics). MAAP #241 (Pacsi et al., 2026) reports ~500 ha inside the reserve, late 2025 to Feb 2026. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_18_placebo.title: The fall stands out in hectares, not for its size
slide_18_placebo.subtitle: Each grey dot: one Peruvian buffer zone given a fake operation in 2019 · orange: the Tambopata buffer zone's real 2019–21 change · net mining additions, after each zone's level and each year's shared change
slide_18_placebo.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. 15 Peruvian buffer zones with mining before 2019 (scaled: 7 with more than 10 ha/yr). Tambopata removed from each fake zone's comparison pool. A rank shows whether the real result stands out; with one target it is not a significance test.

slide_b0_estimates.title: One causal range: 1,453–1,663 ha a year
slide_b0_estimates.subtitle: Estimated change in net mining additions, ha/yr · Tambopata buffer zone · 2019–21 · causal only if the comparison zones show what Tambopata would have done; an upper bound; part of it is pits stopping
slide_b0_estimates.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. 15 Peruvian buffer zones, 2014–25 (zone + year effects and synthetic DiD); Tambopata vs Amarakaeri on the 2014–18 baseline. Fake-2016 test: same model with a fake start in 2016.

slide_b1_stopped_split.title: Stopped land: often water, often mined again within 2 years
slide_b1_stopped_split.subtitle: Stopped land (left the mining class), share by what it became and share mining again within 2 years, period means · four zones · 2016–18, 2019–21, 2022–25 (small numbers under the bars: stopped ha/yr). Numbers on top: share mining again within 2 years.
slide_b1_stopped_split.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), our pixel accounting. Back within 2 years = classifier flicker or re-entry; the last two years cannot be followed up. No image validation sample.

slide_b2_twins.title: Twins: Tambopata at 16%–41% of their pace; trends differed before
slide_b2_twins.subtitle: Left: mining area (stock), index 2018 = 100, 2010–18 (pre-trends rejected, p < 0.001). Right: Amazon Mining Watch new area 2019–21 per year, % of own 2018 area: a different measure, not net additions.
slide_b2_twins.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Col 4 rasters, v3 registry (Tambopata) / MapBiomas Amazonía Col 6 (twins); Amazon Mining Watch new area, area-weighted (comparable to first-time mining, not net). Twins chosen by fixed rules (Ruby's four rules). Different collections: compared as indices, never subtracted.
